home.methodTitle: Every point is earned — and explained
home.methodText: Scores add up from six weighted categories. Privacy points require evidence such as a published independent audit; value points come from real published prices. Affiliate commissions play no part, which is why a VPN with no affiliate program can rank in our top ten.

faq.q: What is the best VPN right now?
faq.a: NordVPN leads our scorecard with 9.1/10 thanks to repeatedly audited no-logs claims, RAM-only servers, a very fast WireGuard-based protocol and a large network. Surfshark (8.7) is the best value if you need many devices, and ExpressVPN (8.6) is the most polished premium option.

Each VPN is scored out of 100 across six categories: speed & performance (25), privacy & security (25), ease of use (15), server network (15), price & value (15) and streaming (5). The full rules are on our methodology page.
No. Some links are affiliate links, but providers cannot buy a position or a score. Mullvad, which has no affiliate program, still ranks in our top ten.

faq.q: Is it legal to use a VPN?
faq.a: In most countries, yes. A few countries ban or restrict VPNs, and illegal activity stays illegal with a VPN. See our VPN legality by country page before you travel.

faq.q: Is a free VPN good enough?
faq.a: Most free VPNs are limited or fund themselves with your data. Proton VPN's free plan is the exception we recommend: no data cap and no ads, but fewer locations and features than paid plans.

legality.metaTitle: Are VPNs Legal? VPN Legality by Country (Updated)
legality.metaDescription: Where VPNs are legal, restricted or banned: a country-by-country overview, updated regularly. Not legal advice.
legality.h1: Are VPNs legal? VPN legality by country
legality.lead: VPNs are legal in most of the world and widely used by businesses, journalists and everyday people. A small number of countries ban or restrict them. This overview helps you check before you use a VPN or travel.
legality.quick: VPNs are legal in most countries, including the US, UK, EU countries, Turkey, India, Japan, Korea, Brazil and Indonesia. They are banned in countries such as North Korea, Turkmenistan and Belarus, and restricted in countries such as China, Russia, Iran and the UAE. Anything illegal without a VPN is still illegal with one.
legality.disclaimer: Laws change and enforcement varies. This page is general information only; check official sources or a local lawyer for your situation. To respect local laws, links to VPN providers are disabled for visitors from countries where VPN use is banned or restricted.
legality.notListed: Country not listed? That usually means VPNs are legal there, but always check local rules.

notes.banned: Using a VPN is prohibited by law.
notes.approved_only: Only VPNs approved or licensed by the government may be used.
notes.unregistered_blocked_ads: Unregistered VPN services are blocked, and promoting VPNs as a way around blocks is prohibited.
notes.restricted_shutdowns: Authorities have restricted or blocked VPN use at times.
notes.registration: VPN use must be registered with or authorised by the telecom regulator.
notes.legitimate_use: VPNs are legal for legitimate purposes, but using one to commit a crime or access prohibited content is illegal.
notes.legal: VPNs are legal. Illegal activity remains illegal with or without a VPN.
notes.legal_sites_blocked: VPNs are legal to use, but access to some VPN providers' websites is blocked.
notes.legal_provider_logs: VPNs are legal to use; VPN providers operating locally must follow data-retention rules.

faq.a: No, not in most countries. VPNs are ordinary security tools used by companies and individuals. A handful of countries ban or restrict them, and using a VPN never makes an illegal activity legal.

faq.q: Can I use a VPN when I travel?
faq.a: Usually yes, but check the rules of the country you are visiting before you travel. In countries where VPNs are restricted, only government-approved services may be allowed.

faq.q: Is it legal to use a VPN for streaming?
faq.a: Using a VPN is generally legal, but streaming services set their own terms of use and may limit content by region. Check the terms of the service you use.

faq.q: Why are VPN links disabled in my country?
faq.a: To respect local laws, we do not link to VPN providers for visitors from countries where VPN use is banned or restricted.

ip.metaTitle: What Is My IP Address? Check Your Public IP & Location
ip.metaDescription: See your public IP address and approximate location instantly, and learn what websites can see about you. Free, no sign-up, nothing stored.
ip.lead: This is the public IP address and approximate location that every website you visit can see.
ip.error: We couldn't look up your IP right now. Please reload the page.
ip.hideTitle: Don't want websites to see this?
ip.hideText: A VPN replaces your IP address with one of its servers, hiding your location from websites and your traffic from your network. Our top-rated VPN is {name}.
ip.quick: Your IP address is a number that identifies your internet connection. Websites use it to estimate your country and city. A VPN hides your real IP address by routing your traffic through one of its servers.
ip.privacy: We look up your IP only to show it to you. It is not logged or stored.

faq.a: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a number assigned to your internet connection so data can find its way to you. Your public IP is usually assigned by your internet provider and shared by the devices on your home network.

faq.q: Can someone find my home address from my IP?
faq.a: Not directly. An IP address usually reveals your internet provider and an approximate city or region. Only your internet provider can link it to your account, typically when legally required.

faq.q: How do I hide my IP address?
faq.a: The easiest way is a reputable VPN, which shows websites the VPN server's IP instead of yours. Tor also hides your IP but is slower.

faq.q: Why does the location look wrong?
faq.a: IP location databases are approximate. Mobile networks, VPNs and corporate networks often appear in a different city or even country.
